script.title: Why Your Loan EMI Won’t Drop Soon #shorts

segments.text: Your home loan EMI is not dropping anytime soon.
Millions of borrowers were betting the Reserve Bank would finally cut interest rates this season.
Instead, retail inflation just punched straight through the danger mark of six point two percent.
By law, the central bank must keep consumer inflation anchored around four percent.
broll_alt: bank vault metal door close up

segments.text: Cutting rates right now pumps more easy cash into the economy, making your daily chai and sabzi even costlier.
segments.broll: boiling indian street chai close up

segments.text: So until grocery bills chill out, banks will not shave a single rupee off your monthly payment.
broll_alt: office worker sitting at desk night

script.loop_line: And as long as inflation stays hot...
script.description: Hoping for an RBI interest rate cut to lower your home loan EMI? With retail inflation breaching the 6% upper limit, the central bank has hit pause on rate cuts. Educational breakdown only. Not financial advice. #personalfinance #inflation #homeloan

facts_to_verify.claim: India's retail inflation breached 6%, straining the RBI's easing cycle.
The RBI inflation mandate targets 4% with an upper tolerance limit of 6%.

script.chosen_candidate: Inflation above 6%, and RBI's easing cycle comes under strain - The New Indian Express
script.why_it_will_work: Every middle-class borrower is eagerly awaiting lower EMIs, and tying high vegetable prices directly to delayed loan relief creates instant relatable curiosity.
